source.title: Is This the Subspace You Are Looking for? An Interpretability Illusion for Subspace Activation Patching
source.authors: Aleksandar Makelov; Georg Lange; Atticus Geiger; Neel Nanda

record.tranche_reason: The study tests subspace activation patching on the IOI task and argues that some apparently causal MLP subspaces are illusory: their effects rely on a causally disconnected component, while patching the full MLP has little or an opposite effect. It also tests how the result varies with intervention location, decomposition, metric, and training data.
record.gate_note: The paper reports IOI patching outcomes in Table 1 and Appendix B.6 and qualitative results on DAS overfitting in Appendix B.7. It also discusses the original circuit and cites results from Wang et al. (2023); those cited results are not recorded as this study's findings. Results on factual recall and rank-1 editing are outside the IOI claim and are not included.
record.test_reason: On GPT-2 small IOI (ABB/BAB), the study probes the position signal that S-Inhibition heads pass to Name Movers. It does this with DAS, gradient directions and full-component patches. Residual-stream directions written by S-Inhibition heads and read by Name Mover queries mediate the signal, which bears on V1's roles. Full MLP8 patching has no effect (-8% FLDD), matching MLP8's exclusion from the circuit. Subspace patching in MLP8, by contrast, yields an illusory mediator. This shows the choice of intervention and metric changes which components appear to carry IOI (V4, V5). The paper argues the subspace method needs extra validation, so T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add that the residual-stream direction is written only by S-Inhibition heads and read via the Name Mover queries, which the authors present as consistent with Wang et al.'s circuit and with MLP8 playing no real role. Their recommendation is to run subspace methods in bottlenecks such as the residual stream and to validate beyond end-to-end patch effects.
record.recipe_differences: Uses DAS to learn 1-dimensional and higher-dimensional subspaces, activation patches, gradient directions, and component/subspace decompositions; it does not reproduce the original full 26-head circuit discovery and validation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effect changes with intervention location (MLP versus residual stream), subspace decomposition (nullspace versus rowspace), intervention size, metric (FLDD versus interchange accuracy), and DAS training-data diversity. The paper also reports greater train than test FLDD when trained on only two names and a fixed template.

fits_no_version.finding: DAS trained on a two-name, fixed-template IOI set overfits: train FLDD exceeds test FLDD. FLDD peaks at layer 8 and neighbouring layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Subspace-search methods for IOI features need diverse training prompts to generalise.

record.problems: Main IOI patch outcomes are reported without uncertainty estimates. The paper's residual-stream causally relevant subspace is a proxy based on Name Mover query matrices. It studies selected directions and patches, not the full circuit's faithfulness, completeness, or minimality. The authors note that DAS overfits on a small dataset and that the MLP subspace result is comparatively modest by interchange accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No additional IOI numerical intervention results were omitted. The Appendix B.7 layer-by-layer small-data results are shown in Figure 17 without tabulated values; the row records only the accompanying qualitative statements.

untested.parts: The full 26-head, 7-class circuit; duplicate-token, induction, previous-token and negative heads; faithfulness, completeness and minimality scores. Only the S-Inhibition to Name Mover position signal and MLP8's exclusion are probed.
Name Movers are not ablated. Backup Name Movers appear only in a footnote conjecture for why vresid beats vgrad.
No other models, sizes, checkpoints or tasks for the IOI circuit. Factual recall in GPT2-XL concerns the illusion, not the circuit.
Does not test whether other circuit-finding methods (e.g. ACDC, path patching variants) recover the whole circuit.
Does not measure circuit-level faithfulness or completeness under different ablations or prompt distributions, nor what fraction of behaviour the circuit explains.
Uses three fixed templates (train vs held-out test), but does not test whether the circuit holds across name orders beyond ABB/BAB, more names, or other formats.

missing.what: A DAS subspace found on random MLP weights, added to MLP8's output, reduces logit difference more than vMLP. The illusory MLP8 attribution is independent of MLP8's content.
vresid and vgrad have cosine similarity about 0.78 (random baseline about 0.03). 91% and 98% of their norm lies in the Name Mover query-relevant subspace. Both separate ABB from BAB well.
Residual-stream DAS solutions are stable, including when trained on a subset of S-Inhibition heads (high cosine similarity).
Model capability on the study's IOI set: about 91% accuracy, mean logit difference about 3.3, correct-over-incorrect in about 99% of examples.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 labels were limits_scope. The results show the evaluation sensitivity V5 describes, so the label is changed to supports; the MLP8 illusion also bears on V4. Rows r20-r23 swap vgrad's rowspace and nullspace values relative to Table 1. r6/r7 are zero by construction and carry no evidence. No uncertainty estimates are reported for Table 1. Factual-recall/ROME results are outside the claim.

versions.untested_parts: Tests selected IOI position-information roles, including writing by S-Inhibition heads, but does not test the complete 26-head, 7-class circuit or the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
Does not ablate main Name Mover heads to test backup-head self-repair.
Does not test whether the same circuit is present in other models, sizes, checkpoints, or tasks.
Does not compare circuit-finding methods for recovery of the claimed circuit. Its comparisons concern interventions and evaluation metrics, not recovery of the full circuit.
Does not test every prompt distribution or establish what fraction of all IOI behavior the original full circuit explains.
Does not test whether the complete 26-head circuit carries IOI across prompt variants or more-name formats; its patching experiments concern a position-information feature and ABB/BAB examples.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 small, ABB/BAB IOI prompts, position signal at the last token after layer 8
relationships.reason: S-Inhibition heads alone write the position direction (r1). Directions in the Name Mover query space mediate it (r12-r13, r16-r18, r20, r26-r29), while full MLP8 patching does nothing (r2-r3). This matches the circuit's S-Inhibition to Name Mover channel.
relationships.display_finding: Only S-inhibition heads wrote the position direction, which acted through name-mover query directions, while patching the full MLP8 had no effect.
